3. **FOS-000003 — Check shared file-helper flush/close completion.** **S; no dependencies; §6.** [file:56](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/file.cpp#L56) and `write_buffer_to_file()` return true after unchecked `fclose()` (E3). Keep destructor/cleanup behavior nonthrowing. **Check:** `/dev/full`, nonexistent destination and successful normal write. Successful close means completion through the OS interface, not power-loss durability. This supplies a truthful primitive for later exporters.

implementation: Keep the existing two- and three-argument bool function definitions and exact signatures in cli/file.hpp; add distinctly named result-returning entrypoints rather than changing signatures or adding default parameters. Use a small plain result with success, an operation enum (none/open/write/flush/close), and raw errno. The result is inspectable without parsing logs and success has none/zero error fields.

Introduce a per-call internal file-operation adapter (open, byte write, flush, close plus context) shared by production stdio and tests; avoid mutable global hooks. Preserve fopen modes w for strings and wb for buffers. String length remains strlen (stops at first NUL); use byte-count writing so string and buffer short writes have an explicit oracle. Preserve native text newline translation.

Capture errno immediately at each failed operation, before flush/close/other cleanup. Reset errno before each adapter operation so stale values cannot be attributed to a new failure; if a failing operation supplies errno=0 retain raw zero as unknown rather than inventing an OS error. Record only the earliest failure. After any successful open, attempt flush then close even after a write error, retaining earliest write/flush errors when cleanup sets different errno values. Invalidate owned handle before close so failure cannot cause retry/double close. Close failure alone must fail.

Any owned-handle destructor/cleanup is noexcept and does not publish errors by throwing; explicit completion returns the authoritative result. No new allocations or exception dependence in write/finalization path. Legacy bool wrappers use the structured result, return its success, and restore its raw first errno on failure after cleanup.

Add test/file_helper_test.cpp with explicit checks active under NDEBUG; one test executable dispatches named scenarios. Register each scenario separately with CTest, including both helper kinds. Fault adapter counts every operation and marks consumed handles; fail tests on double close or use after close. Supply distinct errno values per failure and cleanup clobbering controls.

Add a legacy caller fixture using only baseline declarations and exact bool function-pointer types. Register candidate roundtrip and completion modes with CTest. The fixture must compile against extracted input-revision file.hpp and candidate file.cpp, then run candidate successful and failure modes. Its Linux dev-full mode also runs against unchanged input file.cpp and must reject both historical false-success results; keep old and new evidence separate.

Register new tests in test/CMakeLists.txt with FOSSILIZE_TESTS, platform guards only for /dev/full, project exception/sanitizer compile/link flags, private per-test working directories and finite TIMEOUT. Prefer compiling cli/file.cpp directly into the lightweight helper targets so no GPU/CLI dependencies are needed for the new tests, while full CLI/layer builds still verify unchanged callers.

Update local-docs/verification.md with test inventory, API/compatibility guarantees and explicit platform limitations. Do not change unconditional mandatory harness-suite guidance to evade it. All source/tests/docs stay in the implementation commit; transient build/probe outputs stay outside source.

Report source compatibility as preserved for the two legacy functions using unchanged old declarations plus compile/run fixtures; no all-callers generalization. Binary: exact legacy symbols retained, but static cli-utils has no general supported C++ binary ABI claim, so no prebuilt-consumer ABI claim. Protocol: no wire/file format or machine-output schema change introduced here. Behavioral: normal/empty contents, truncation, text/binary distinction and initial open/write failures preserved; formerly false-success flush/close cases intentionally return false with the first error. Do not silently propagate this into unrelated tool exit redesign.

Implementer and both fresh checkers run real bounded commands against committed candidate, exact planned IDs and mappings. No mandatory skipped/unavailable result counts as accepted. Apply the direct user platform scope decision: Linux matrix and portable injected tests are mandatory; native Windows execution is optional, not_run/unverified for this run, and must be explicitly disclosed in final evidence and the PR. Portable Linux execution must never be mapped to Windows execution or claimed as native validation. Preserve original AC1 verbatim. Prior implementation reports are historical evidence only; plan v2 requires renewed work-unit checking and separate final checking at the exact candidate/base/plan tuple.

The coordinator may supply external verification drivers for each exact configuration or harness group; workers request canonical command-intent for each top-level verification command before execution. The driver must preserve the listed commands/assertions, record actual per-process statuses, and enforce <=600-second deadlines on each build/test process. Inspection calls do not require source changes or nested canonical writes. At most three harness group processes concurrently.

Fresh checker working directories, build directories, baseline output directories and harness evidence directories may be relocated to fresh absolute paths outside source without changing gate IDs, test IDs, flags, assertions, test inventories, deadlines or the exact candidate. Record resolved commands/cwd and compiler configuration. Expected CLI/layer-enabled inventory is 91 Linux tests and 87 registered Windows tests before optional runtime layer integration; 87 is a registration expectation, not native execution evidence.
non_goals: No fsync/fdatasync/FlushFileBuffers, atomic replacement, rollback of partial files or power-loss durability promise.
No change to load_buffer_from_file, exporters, aggregate CLI exit policies, databases, capture finalization, logging schemas, process control or complete observability compliance.
No general C++ binary ABI guarantee or wire/protocol compatibility claim beyond no protocol change; no GPU/driver compilation, cache reuse, Steam or layer runtime claim.

Legacy identity: `FOS-000003`. Original source: [immutable historical definition](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/73f891d6c0cf498ac92e804d7d0f0cd344a083f5/local-docs/reviews/observability-sweep.md).

Shared requirements and grouping: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/8. All original criteria below remain required. Source status statements below describe their historical revision; current delivery evidence is recorded separately. Original relative links are resolved below.

## Original definition (verbatim)

3. **FOS-000003 — Check shared file-helper flush/close completion.** **S; no dependencies; §6.** [file:56](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/file.cpp#L56) and `write_buffer_to_file()` return true after unchecked `fclose()` (E3). Return failure for write/flush/close errors, preserving the first raw error and operation. Keep destructor/cleanup behavior nonthrowing. **Check:** `/dev/full`, nonexistent destination and successful normal write. Successful close means completion through the OS interface, not power-loss durability. This supplies a truthful primitive for later exporters.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Unit tests with injectable file operations:** Open, short-write, flush and close failures each return failure; when several occur, the first error and its operation survive cleanup. Close is attempted exactly once for each opened handle.
   - **Filesystem integration tests:** E3 fails on Linux /dev/full; a portable injected close-error case covers other platforms. Normal and empty writes succeed and read back byte-for-byte; no result claims stronger durability than tested flush/close completion.
